summary: Jinzhang Peng worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He served as deputy director of history at Wuhan University (~1963–1986), and at Dunhuang Academy as dean of the archaeological institute (~1986) and researcher (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1904 to ~1907. He held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1917–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1943). He later held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1964–1977), University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1991).

Jiro Murata worked in history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1917 to ~1920 and later held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College, from ~1962 to ~1967.

Jiro Sugiyama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1954), specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1978–1994), ICPBS (~1996–2004), and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara. He served as a professor at the University of Calcutta and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and held a post as professor emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1917–1920) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen (Ph.D.). A philosopher and Indologist, he taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, Emory, and Temple University (~1986–2007), and founded Husserl Studies.
Jitsushyu Oshika specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and later served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896), focusing on sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada from ~1970 to ~1989 and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan earned a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera (attested 2023). Working in computational linguistics and Indology, he held posts at IIT Kanpur, Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. He taught at Peking University (1942–1964) and served as director of the Institute of World Religions (1964–1986) and honorary director of the National Library of China (1987–2005).

Jiyu-Kennett studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji, training under Seck Kim Seng, Keidō Chisan Kōho, and Suigan Yogo. She served as head priest at Unpukuji (~1968–1969) and founded Shasta Abbey, serving as abbess (~1970–1996).
Joachim Friedrich Sprockhoff worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Otto Schrader and Helmuth von Glasenapp until 1960.

Joachim Gentz specializes in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and held positions as Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.

Joachim Heidrich was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Walter Ruben (1948–1958). He held posts at the Zentralinstitut für Geschichte (1981–1989) and Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (~1992–1995).

Joachim Menant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Caen Normandy. He held posts at the University of Paris and became a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1888.
Joachim Prandstetter studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Vienna, earning his Magister by 1994, and studied under Gerhard Oberhammer (attested 1994).
